text:
[curious] Why Are There Two Minecrafts?
[excited] Say your redstone farm works on Java. Then you open Bedrock, and it breaks. But why did they even make two versions?
[thoughtful] And why not just merge them into one?
[confident] Well Java is the original code minecraft was written in but doesn't run on consoles or phones, so Bedrock was built in another programming language.
[serious] Now every feature gets built twice, and both have to match. This is what you call parity.
[amused] Now if you merge them, millions of worlds and mods stop working. So you'd break the thing players love most.
[laughs] [proud] This is why the comments are still fighting about it.
[proud] It's one game on the box. But It's two games in the code.
